summary: The Tool Databases finding now measures filesystem readability only and explicitly states that SQLite integrity and mmap were not checked; no message claims a verified database or mmap readiness. Missing database paths emit an INFO finding that discloses nothing could be assessed, and unreadable paths keep a WARN with the same limit disclosure. The Delta Cache finding states writability factually instead of promising sub-10ms readiness and now surfaces a visible WARN when the cache directory cannot be created; probe files remain cleaned up and only Thermal's own cache is touched. README and project.jsonc no longer advertise mmap, transcript-ceiling, or pricing-cache checks. The historical probe was updated to the new narrow expectation while the original audit log is preserved.

cases.evidence: TestAuditDatabaseReadabilityClaim: plain text at state_5.sqlite is readable and may PASS only under the readability label; the message contains no 'verified'/'mmap-ready' wording and explicitly says SQLite integrity and mmap were not checked. Missing paths emit INFO 'not assessed'; an unreadable path (mode 0000) emits WARN with the same disclosure. The updated audit probe prints the narrow message and passes.

TestAuditCacheFailureVisible: a regular file at ~/.cache/thermal causes a visible WARN ('could not be created') and leaves fixture bytes unchanged; a writable cache PASSes with a factual writability message (no 'sub-10ms' or 'ready' claims) and removes its .audit_probe_* file.
go test -race ./internal/audit ./internal/render -run Audit exits 0; README audit paragraph and project.jsonc capability wording now describe readability-only checks with updated lastEdit.
